assessment.nobel_worthiness: The localisation of gamma-ray bursts to arcminutes with the BeppoSAX instruments, followed by the X-ray, optical and radio afterglows and redshift measurements, settled the decades-old question of whether bursts are Galactic or cosmological. This is a clean, instrument-driven discovery that opened a field and changed the understanding of the most energetic explosions; the chain from wide-field monitor to rapid pointing to ground-based follow-up is a textbook case of an experimental breakthrough.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX Wide Field Cameras and Gamma-Ray Burst Monitor and the first X-ray afterglow; Kulkarni's group delivered the decisive optical and radio counterparts and redshift-based distance scale. The three names cover the instrument, the X-ray afterglow and the ground-based follow-up. Other contributors (for example the optical discovery teams and the BeppoSAX mission team) may deserve consideration, so the split of credit is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: The discovery dates from 1997 and has been confirmed by Swift, Fermi and many later missions, with the cosmological origin and the link to collapsars and compact mergers now well established. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the optical-afterglow credit should go to Kulkarni's group alone or be shared with other teams that obtained the first optical counterpart and spectra.
Several key figures are deceased or elderly, which may limit the available configuration; I have not verified their current status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies with the cubic-kilometre IceCube detector opened neutrino astronomy as a new window, and the later association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane strengthen the case. It is an extraordinary instrumentation achievement at the South Pole.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove IceCube as principal investigator and is the only name supplied, which gives a single-laureate configuration. The discovery is nonetheless a product of a very large collaboration, and I cannot say from the supplied text whether a fair prize can rest on one name or whether other scientists made decisive contributions that are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: The 2013 evidence has been confirmed in multiple channels and by independent analyses, and source identification continues to mature. The field is still developing but the core discovery is secure.
uncertainties: Credit for a collaboration-scale discovery rests on one individual, and the committee would need to weigh the roles of the other IceCube leaders and of the AMANDA precursor.
Origins of most of the diffuse flux remain unidentified, so the astrophysical interpretation is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a nonzero theta13 completed the three-flavour mixing picture and opened the way to leptonic CP-violation searches. It was a decisive, precise experimental result with clear physical meaning, obtained with reactor and accelerator neutrinos in complementary ways.
assessment.attribution: Wang and Luk are tied to Daya Bay (spokesperson and project leadership) and Nishikawa to T2K, which first showed electron-neutrino appearance. Reactor-based RENO and Double Chooz were also decisive contributors, and the supplied credit omits their leaders, so the allocation is contested and the three-person limit is tight.
assessment.maturity: The result dates from 2011-2012 and has been confirmed by several independent experiments with improving precision, so the physics is mature. The 2015 prize already honoured neutrino oscillations, which weighs on timing.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit between Daya Bay, RENO, Double Chooz and T2K is unresolved.
The prior award for neutrino oscillations may make a further neutrino prize less likely to be seen as urgent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene combines a striking theoretical prediction of flat bands with the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity, and it created the field of moire quantum materials. Originality and impact are very high and the experiments are elegant in their control of a single parameter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle, and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 observations. Andrei's group contributed early scanning-probe evidence of flat bands and also has a claim, so one name must be left out; the choice is delicate but a theory-plus-experiment configuration is workable.
assessment.maturity: The experimental results have been reproduced widely and many related platforms exist, but the mechanism of superconductivity is still debated, and the field is evolving fast.
uncertainties: Eva Y. Andrei's contribution may be judged equal to one of the proposed names.
The superconducting pairing mechanism is still not settled, which may argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks using the magic-wavelength idea have reached fractional uncertainties near the 1e-18 level and underpin tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. This is precision instrumentation of the kind I value, with broad scientific reach.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and Ye's group drove the strontium clocks to record accuracy and stability. The two-name configuration looks fair, though trapped-ion clock pioneers and others contributed to optical clocks more generally.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks around the world agree and keep improving, and the 2005 prize covered the frequency comb, so this builds on a recognised base. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: The separation from the earlier frequency-comb and single-ion clock prizes needs care.
Whether the committee prefers the concept (Katori) or the performance (Ye and others) is a matter of judgement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays opened the nanohertz gravitational-wave band, and the 2023 evidence for a stochastic background is an important first result with astrophysical implications for supermassive black-hole binaries. The technique is a long-baseline, long-duration experiment of high originality.
assessment.attribution: Kramer (EPTA), McLaughlin (NANOGrav) and Manchester (PPTA) lead the three main arrays, which is a natural geographic and collaborative spread. The credit here rests on leadership of collaborations, and the individual intellectual contributors (including early proposals of timing arrays) are not fully represented.
assessment.maturity: The detection is at about the 3-4 sigma level in the individual arrays with combined analyses still ongoing, and the origin of the signal is not yet settled. This looks premature for now.
uncertainties: Statistical significance is below the conventional discovery threshold in some analyses, and the source (binaries versus new physics) is unresolved.
Early theoretical and methodological pioneers are not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect transformed condensed matter physics and led to a new classification of phases. The theory and the HgTe experiment form a compelling prediction-then-confirmation story.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical proposal, and Molenkamp's group realised the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not in the credited names. Hasan's ARPES work on three-dimensional topological insulators is a separate and strong claim, and a three-person limit forces a difficult choice; the credit is genuinely compound.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by many groups and materials, so very mature, and in fact arguably long overdue.
uncertainties: The role of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and of Fu and Kane in three dimensions is not reflected in the supplied names.
A compound discovery whose two-dimensional and three-dimensional parts may need different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of quantized conductance steps in ballistic point contacts demonstrated mesoscopic quantum transport in a clean and instructive way, and became a building block for quantum dots, spin qubits and later anyon and Majorana experiments. The concept is simple and the effect is textbook-level.
assessment.attribution: The two 1988 experiments by the Delft-Philips group (van Wees) and the Cambridge group (Wharam, Pepper) were independent and simultaneous, which supports a fair configuration; the theoretical interpretation by Landauer and others is not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely reproduced, with a stable interpretation. The risk is that recognition may be thought too late or too narrow compared with the larger impact of the 2D electron gas prizes already given.
uncertainties: The relative importance of the Landauer-type theory versus the experiments is outside the credited names.
Some of the experimental leaders may be deceased, which I have not verified.
